text:
miriam: Heads-up — Product just confirmed Citrine (65B) soft-launch in 14 days. Benchmarks from the trial cluster show ~2.8x tokens/sec compared to our current large-model baseline and about ~1.9x GPU-hours per 1M tokens because of longer average contexts. We need a short impact projection (GPU headroom, reserve vs burst cost, region constraints) and an ops plan for the launch window.

miriam: Quick bench dump (sanitized):
```
model: citrine-65b
seq: 512 median
p99 latency: 680ms (single-stream)
tokens/s per instance: 2.1k -> 5.8k (2.8x)
gpu-hours / 1M tokens: 5.2 -> 9.9 (1.9x)
KV cache blowup on long-chat workloads: ~+12% memory foot print
```

noah: If tokens/sec per request jumps 2.8x, what's the projected cluster-wide tps->tokens/sec mapping? Do we have an estimate of concurrent requests shape?

miriam: Current peak (baseline) = 1.2M tokens/sec across hosted fleet during busy hour. If adoption drives a 2.0x traffic multiplier on top of the model efficiency delta (conservative), peak tokens/sec becomes: 1.2M * 2.0 * 2.8 = ~6.7M tokens/sec.

miriam: Rough capacity math: our optimized A100 equivalent can sustain ~40k tokens/sec under our production kernel with batching and kv-cache in place (observed avg). So 6.7M / 40k ≈ 168 GPUs required at peak for hosted. Current available pooled capacity (all regions) = 220 GPUs, but 40% is reserved for other commitments and Dedicated customers => usable headroom ≈ 132 GPUs. Gap ≈ 36 GPUs.

raj: Ballpark cost numbers: on on-demand spot-like cloud pricing we charge-basis is $1.8 / GPU-hour equivalent for running cost (internal blended). Adding 36 GPUs continuous at peak hours (assume 6 hours/day peak) => 36 * 6 * $1.8 ≈ $389/day incremental for the peak window. But that ignores broader tail and pre-warm churn. If we reserve capacity to cover 24/7 for launch week (worst case), 36 * 24 * $1.8 ≈ $1.55k/day. Also consider buffer for autoscaling safety + 20% => ~43 GPUs.

felix: Two important ops notes: 1) Batching improvement: we can squeeze 1.25x tokens/sec by tuning batching window and enabling aggressive microbatch packing for this model, might reduce gap by ~13%. 2) Quantization: we have a validated 8-bit path for Citrine that reduces GPU memory allowing +10% more instances per GPU (not always for latency-sensitive flows). Combined could reduce effective GPU gap to single digits. Need a validation pass for p99 regression.

olga: Regional constraints: ap-southeast has only 18 usable GPUs right now; eu-west has 36. If traffic skews to APAC on global launch day we might run out regionally even if global pool is OK. Network egress: Citrine replies are 30% larger on average (longer outputs) — that increases egress and may trigger peering throttles in eu-west. We should plan region fallbacks and per-region rate limiting.

tara: Ops rollout suggestion: staged canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with automatic rollback on p99>900ms or error-rate>1.2%. Also suggest enabling dedicated pool for enterprise customers to avoid SLA blips.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment created: https://deploys.internal/release/citrine-canary (5% slot) :rocket:

noah: Action items I propose:
- short benchmark run with quantized build on staging (owner: felix) — 24h
- update autoscaler knobs to prefer queueing over rejecting at 90% util (owner: miriam) — today
- reserve 48 GPUs in us-west-2 for launch week if finance signs off (owner: raj) — EOD
- add region fallback policy to route EU->US when EU headroom < 10% and inform product (owner: olga) — tomorrow
- run network egress smoke to verify peering headroom (owner: olga) — today
- define canary rollback thresholds in console (owner: tara) — today

raj: Reserve vs burst note: Reserved instances reduce unit cost by ~22% but require commit. For a one-week launch boost it's cheaper to burst if capacity is available and we accept slightly higher per-hour cost. If we expect sustained elevated demand 3+ months then reserve. Finance asks: what is probability of sustained demand? Product says 40% chance. Recommend hybrid: reserve 24 GPUs (minimum) + allow burst up to +36 via cloud spot/partner pool.

miriam: I'll schedule a 30-min ops sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to confirm numbers and lock the reserve decision. If quant validation looks good we'll enable 8-bit path only for requests with latency headroom.

noah: One more thing — telemetry hooks: please add two quick eval prompts (short + long) to post-launch evals to catch any generation quality regressions that correlate with quantization/batching.

miriam: Agreed. I'll add those evals and wire alerts if quality drift > 2% on our prompt set.

felix: I'll start the quant/staging run now and post a short bench report in this thread when done.

olga: Running egress smoke now, will tag infra-alert if we hit peering thresholds.

miriam: Perfect. Summary: conservative peak gap ~36 GPUs, potential reduction with batching/quant to ~<10 GPUs. Plan: hybrid reserve(24) + burst, staged canary, region fallbacks, and telemetry. Meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT. :white_check_mark:
